fields.mechanism: A solenoid valve physically simulates controlled pressure conditions against a water pressure sensor, enabling verification of occlusion detection accuracy relative to a fixed 20 Psi threshold before real clinical use.
fields.intervention: Embed a micro solenoid valve and a calibrated reference pressure chamber into the infusion pump's downstream fluid path; at startup and at periodic intervals during infusion, the valve momentarily applies a known calibrated back-pressure step (below the 20 Psi harm threshold) to the in-line occlusion pressure sensor, and the pump's processor compares the sensor reading against the expected value, auto-recalibrating or locking out the pump if drift exceeds a tight error margin.
fields.expected_effect: Continuous in-situ verification of occlusion sensor calibration eliminates the sensor drift (up to 58-71% error observed in uncalibrated devices) that causes delayed detection, so the occlusion alarm triggers at the true pressure rise before harmful medication or fluid delivery deviation reaches the patient.

fields.mechanism: Pressure buildup from a downstream occlusion is transmitted through the fluid column and physically acts on a pressure-responsive element (a water pressure sensor) while a solenoid valve modulates the pressure path; inverting this, the pressure itself becomes the actuator — the occlusion-induced pressure rise passively drives a flow-path change instead of merely being sensed and reported.
fields.intervention: Install an inline, passive pressure-actuated diversion valve between the pump and the patient, set to the 20 Psi occlusion threshold established by ECRI: when downstream occlusion pressure builds, the rising pressure mechanically (passively) shifts the valve seat to divert flow into a reservoir/bypass line and structurally interrupt delivery to the patient

fields.mechanism: Direct hydraulic pressure transduction — a water pressure sensor in the fluid line detects the pressure rise caused by an occlusion and transmits the reading to a processor that compares it against a calibrated occlusion threshold (20 Psi per ECRI), enabling detection of the blockage from the pressure signal itself.
fields.intervention: Integrate a calibrated inline pressure sensor immediately downstream of the pump mechanism (before the patient line segment) that continuously measures line pressure and triggers the occlusion alarm as soon as pressure crosses the validated threshold, with the sensor's error margin verified during annual recalibration using a dual-channel analyzer with a solenoid valve simulating occlusion pressure.
fields.expected_effect: Occlusion is detected from the pressure buildup in the segment between pump and patient before the delivered volume deviation propagates to the patient, converting delayed downstream detection into upstream pressure-based detection with a quantified, recalibratable sensor error margin.
fields.falsification_test: Bench-test the modified pump by inducing a downstream occlusion at set distances from the patient port while measuring (a) time from occlusion onset to alarm and (b) volume delivered past the occlusion point before alarm; the intervention fails if the alarm triggers after the pressure exceeds the 20 Psi threshold by more than the sensor's documented error margin, or if fluid deviation reaches the simulated patient port before the alarm fires.
fields.mechanism_source_span: The research employs a water pressure sensor to detect occlusions and a solenoid valve to simulate pressure conditions.

fields.mechanism: Fluidic pressure transduction coupled with electromagnetic actuation: a water pressure sensor detects occlusion-induced line pressure against a 20 Psi threshold, while a solenoid valve electromagnetically simulates pressure conditions to verify the sensing path, with a microcontroller processing sensor output in real time.
fields.intervention: Integrate an inline water pressure sensor in the pump's downstream fluid path, wired to the pump microcontroller, paired with a small solenoid valve that periodically closes to electromagnetically generate a known back-pressure; the microprocessor compares measured pressure rise against the 20 Psi occlusion threshold and triggers the occlusion alarm as pressure climbs toward that limit, while the solenoid self-test confirms the sensor responds correctly before each infusion.
fields.expected_effect: Downstream occlusion is detected from the pressure-rise signature before delivered volume deviates harmfully, and periodic solenoid-driven pressure simulation catches sensor drift (the paper found device error margins from 2.84% to 71.26%), so degraded sensors are flagged at startup rather than failing silently during infusion.

fields.mechanism: Occlusion-induced line pressure is transduced by a water pressure sensor into an electrical signal, which is processed against a defined 20 Psi occlusion threshold, with a solenoid valve generating simulated pressure conditions to verify sensor response accuracy.
fields.intervention: Embed a calibrated in-line pressure sensor in the infusion pump's fluid path just upstream of the patient, set to alarm at the ECRI 20 Psi occlusion threshold, and add a periodic self-test routine in which an internal solenoid valve briefly simulates occlusion pressure to verify the sensor's calibration drift before each infusion, so the alarm threshold remains accurate and triggers at the true onset of pressure rise rather than after a drifted, delayed threshold crossing.
fields.expected_effect: The alarm fires at the first calibrated pressure deviation indicating downstream occlusion, before the pressure (and corresponding medication/fluid delivery deviation) accumulates to harmful levels, eliminating the delayed-detection failure caused by unverified sensor drift.
fields.falsification_test: Bench test comparing two identical pumps, one with the solenoid-valve self-calibration routine and one without: deliberately detune the occlusion sensor by 15%, then create a gradual downstream occlusion with a syringe simulator while measuring time-to-alarm and delivered-volume deviation at alarm.
